headline: National Park Pass Required for Highway 93 North
reservation: A valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass or daily entry fee is required for all vehicles traveling or stopping on the Kootenay Parkway. While entry is generally open, front-country campsites must be reserved months in advance through the Parks Canada Reservation Service.

days.title: The Vermilion Range

stops.name: Marble Canyon
stops.detail: Cross several bridges over a deep limestone gorge where the Tokumm Creek has carved dramatic patterns into the rock.

stops.name: Paint Pots
stops.detail: Walk the short trail to the ochre beds, naturally occurring mineral springs historically significant to the Ktunaxa people.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from Banff to the park gate; traffic varies at the junction.
days.note: Morning light is best for photographing the vibrant orange clay of the Paint Pots.

days.title: Continental Divide to Hot Springs

stops.name: Numa Falls
stops.detail: View the powerful glacial runoff of the Vermilion River from the accessible roadside viewpoint.

stops.name: Radium Hot Springs
stops.detail: Soak in the mineral-rich waters situated within the dramatic Sinclair Canyon rock walls near the southern gate.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours of total driving time to reach the southern end of the park.
days.note: Radium Hot Springs pool hours are seasonal; check the Parks Canada site for current facility maintenance windows.

days.title: Sinclair Canyon and Valley Views
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Radium Hot Springs

stops.name: Olive Lake
stops.detail: Stop at this small, crystal-clear lake on the Sinclair Pass for a quiet boardwalk loop and birdwatching.

stops.name: Kootenay Valley Viewpoint
stops.detail: Capture the expansive vistas of the Mitchell and Vermilion ranges from this elevated roadside pull-off.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes for the winding ascent through Sinclair Pass.
days.note: Watch for bighorn sheep on the road near the Radium park entrance; they are frequently present on the tarmac.

intel.title: The Service Gap
intel.text: There is no fuel, food, or reliable cell service along the 100km stretch of Highway 93 South between Castle Junction and Radium Hot Springs. Top up in Banff or Radium before entering the park.

intel.title: Disconnected Corridor
intel.text: The Kootenay Parkway is a notorious dead zone for mobile devices. Ensure you have physical maps or downloaded GPS data for navigation and emergency contacts.

intel.title: Wildlife Crossing
intel.text: This park is a critical corridor for wolves and grizzly bears; speed limits are strictly enforced to protect transit. Dusk travel requires extreme caution due to low visibility and high animal activity.

intel.title: Winter Travel Requirements
intel.text: From October to April, winter tires or chains are legally required to traverse the Kootenay Parkway. Check the DriveBC portal for updates on avalanche control closures near the Vermilion Pass.

intel.title: Canyon Lot Constraints
intel.text: Marble Canyon is the most visited site in the park; its lot often fills by 10 AM in July. Consider visiting the Paint Pots first and returning to the canyon later in the afternoon.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at YXC (Cranbrook) or YYC (Calgary), purchase groceries in Invermere or Banff, and check in at Radium.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for the parkway, but large RVs should be aware of steep grades and sharp turns in Sinclair Canyon.
plan.goldenHour: Kootenay Valley Viewpoint for wide-angle sunset light over the Rockies; check seasonal tables.
